# Inside the Data Center Boom: Understanding the Massive Infrastructure That Supports AI

First listed: 2025-10-22 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Inside the Data Center Boom: Understanding the Massive Infrastructure That Supports AI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G121VNcu0dg) - 2025-10-22
- [Substack: Inside the Data Center Boom: Understanding the Massive Infrastructure That Supports AI](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/inside-the-data-center-boom-understanding-d0b) - 2025-10-26

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Nick Del Deo explains the distinct economics of data-center property, interconnection hubs, GPU clouds and fiber. The strongest framework separates recurring cash metrics from expansion capex and models CoreWeave contract-level lifetime returns rather than applying peer EBITDA multiples. He expects eventual competition and power supply to reduce scarcity returns but avoids a precise collapse date. Later Equinix growth was stronger than the reported early 2026 plan, while Lumen's legacy decline remained visible.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Map property ownership, equipment ownership and customer obligations separately.
- Distinguish network effects from temporary physical scarcity.
- Value GPU projects over equipment life, including capex, financing, renewals and residual value.
- Lifetime NPV per invested dollar is not an annual return on capital.
- Check final user latency separately from latency inside a training cluster.
- Deduplicate utility requests and distinguish planned, contracted and energized power.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Capital cost per MW excluding IT equipment
- REIT taxable income versus AFFO and cash flow
- Interconnection-hub network effects
- ROIC minus cost of capital and reinvestment volume
- CoreWeave GPU contract DCF and $65 valuation
- Power requests versus realized load
- Lumen conduit value and Cogent wavelength revenue

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman interviews Nick Del Deo. Most forecasts and valuation estimates belong to Del Deo; Eisman asks clarifying questions and restates accounting concepts.
- Opening montage repeats body claims.
- All 1771 caption lines were read.
- Nick Del Deo and company names are frequently garbled.
- Recording appears materially earlier than October 22 publication: Core Scientific bid is described as recent and CoreWeave quoted near $90. Exact date not established.
- The $40b equipment figure against a $14b-$15b contract may be a caption or spoken-number error and is not silently corrected.
- The 2025 $5.3b revenue and 2026 AFFO path are forecasts at the time, not realized premises.
